[curious, lively, starts speaking immediately] There is no lead in your pencil. There never was. It is graphite and clay, baked hard like pottery. In the fifteen hundreds, shepherds in England found a shiny black rock. They called it lead, and the name stuck. Today, powdered graphite and clay are mixed into a dark dough, pressed out into long thin rods, and fired in a hot kiln. Here is the trick. More clay makes a harder, lighter line. More graphite makes it softer, darker, and smudgier. The rods are glued between two grooved slats of cedar, then a blade slices the sandwich into pencils. No lead anywhere.
